assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology, from proglucagon processing and the incretin effect to receptor agonists that lower glucose and body weight, is a rare case of basic hormone biology becoming a transformative therapy across diabetes, obesity and cardiovascular and renal risk. Originality and clarity of the physiological chain are high, and the clinical impact is already very large.
assessment.attribution: Holst established the physiology and secretion of the incretin hormones, Drucker defined the biology of GLP-1 and its therapeutic exploitation, and Mojsov's identification of the active GLP-1(7-37) form is a decisive molecular contribution. Knudsen's pharmaceutical development of long-acting analogues is also major, so the three-person limit forces a hard choice; priority disputes around the peptide work remain.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed independently by many large randomized trials over more than a decade, with a stable interpretation; recognition is timely and arguably urgent.
uncertainties: Allocation among four credited names is unresolved, notably between academic discovery and industrial drug development.
Long-term safety and the full breadth of benefits are still being characterized, though this does not weaken the core discovery.
I rely on recalled knowledge of the priority history and have not verified it independently.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Showing that TNF is a dominant driver of synovial inflammation and that its blockade controls rheumatoid arthritis changed the treatment of chronic inflammatory disease, and established the principle that a single cytokine can be a therapeutic target in a complex immune-mediated disease. The concept was original at the time and the impact on Crohn's disease, psoriasis and spondyloarthritis is lasting.
assessment.attribution: Feldmann and Maini led the translational path from the cytokine cascade in rheumatoid synovium to the first anti-TNF clinical trials, so the two-person credit is coherent and well supported. Others, including the TNF cloning and antibody-engineering communities, contributed, and the supplied credit omits them.
assessment.maturity: Over 25 years of clinical experience, multiple independent agents and biosimilars; the interpretation is stable and recognition is mature. I note my own field is rheumatology and have tried to weigh this on the evidence alone.
uncertainties: The relative weight of the TNF identification and antibody-engineering contributions versus the clinical concept is a possible dispute.
Possible perception of closeness to my own field; I have not treated this as evidence of merit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetically engineered T cells that redirect immunity against cancer have produced durable remissions in refractory B-cell leukemias and lymphomas and now myeloma, and open a new therapeutic modality. The discovery has substantial originality and a clear causal chain from receptor design to patient benefit.
assessment.attribution: Sadelain contributed the foundational CAR design with costimulation, June the clinical translation and the first durable remissions in leukemia, and Rosenberg the adoptive cell transfer and gene-modified T-cell concepts. Other contributors, such as Eshhar, Gross, Kuwana and Finney, complicate a clean three-person configuration.
assessment.maturity: Several approved products and years of follow-up confirm efficacy in hematological malignancy; durability, toxicity and solid-tumor application are still maturing. Timely, though some argue for more time.
uncertainties: Priority among early chimeric-receptor pioneers is contested.
Solid-tumor efficacy and long-term safety remain unproven.
Possible secondary malignancy signals add uncertainty about the final assessment.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The rational inhibition of BCR-ABL turned chronic myeloid leukemia from a fatal disease into a manageable chronic condition and proved the concept of molecularly targeted cancer therapy. Importance, clarity and lasting impact are exceptional.
assessment.attribution: Lydon led the compound discovery, Druker the clinical development and the demonstration of selectivity, and Sawyers the resistance mechanisms and second-generation inhibitors; the three-person configuration is well matched to the credited names. Rowley and the Philadelphia chromosome and Witte, Baltimore and others on ABL biology predate this work and have already been recognized in part elsewhere.
assessment.maturity: More than two decades of survival data and robust independent confirmation; the recognition is mature rather than premature, and it has already received major prizes.
uncertainties: It is not a novel mechanism in basic biology terms, and the prize committee may prefer foundational oncogene work.
Relative weight of discovery chemistry versus clinical proof of concept is debatable.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The discovery of TOR as the target of rapamycin and the cellular growth and nutrient-sensing network it organizes is a conceptual advance in cell physiology with links to cancer, diabetes, aging and immunosuppression. Impact on how nutrient signaling is understood is lasting and wide.
assessment.attribution: Hall's identification of TOR in yeast and demonstration of its conserved role is the decisive foundation. Schreiber's work on the FKBP12-rapamycin complex and Sabatini's work on mammalian mTOR are important but more incremental or complicating, and the Sabatini credit may be contentious, so a single-laureate proposal is the cleanest configuration.
assessment.maturity: Extensively confirmed in yeast, flies and mammals over three decades, though therapeutic payoff beyond transplantation and some oncology uses is still developing.
uncertainties: Whether a one-person award is acceptable given others' contributions.
Mammalian mTOR credit, including Brown, Snyder and Sabatini, is not fully resolved in the supplied credit.
Some of the clinical promise remains unrealized.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The unfolded protein response defined a new intracellular signaling pathway from the endoplasmic reticulum to the nucleus, with relevance to secretory-cell physiology, neurodegeneration, diabetes and cancer. The discovery is original, mechanistically clear and of broad significance.
assessment.attribution: Walter and Mori independently and complementarily defined the Ire1-Hac1/XBP1 pathway, so a two-person credit is coherent and natural; Kozutsumi, Cox and Ron could also be considered by some.
assessment.maturity: Strong confirmation across eukaryotes, with the mechanism stable for 25 years; the disease-treatment translation is still emerging, so recognition would be for the basic discovery.
uncertainties: Therapeutic impact remains limited so far.
Contributions of others in the ER stress field, such as Ron and Harding on PERK, might be considered for inclusion.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Antisense correction of SMN2 splicing produced nusinersen, a disease-modifying therapy for a previously lethal infantile neuromuscular disease, and validated splice-switching oligonucleotides as a therapeutic class. This is a clear case of mechanism-based therapy.
assessment.attribution: Krainer defined the splicing regulation and the ISS-N1 target concept and Bennett developed the antisense chemistry and drug; the two-person credit is compact and appropriate, though Hua and Singh and the SMN gene discovery by Melki and Lefebvre are also relevant.
assessment.maturity: Approved in 2016 with years of clinical follow-up; the interpretation is stable, though it is a relatively recent and narrow-indication therapy and the broader antisense field is still maturing.
uncertainties: Whether the prize would be seen as recognizing a drug more than a general principle.
Credit for the original SMN gene discovery sits outside this candidate.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: BCL-2 revealed that cancer can arise through blocked cell death rather than only increased proliferation, and the family became the basis of BH3 mimetic therapy such as venetoclax. The conceptual advance was major and the translational follow-through is now clear.
assessment.attribution: Cory and Adams cloned and characterized the translocated gene and the family, while Vaux showed that BCL-2 blocks cell death. Strasser is also a key contributor, and Korsmeyer, Tsujimoto and Cleary were part of the discovery, so credit is spread widely and a three-person limit is constraining.
assessment.maturity: Strong independent confirmation, with an approved targeted therapy for CLL and related leukemias; recognition would be timely, though apoptosis has been recognized before (2002).
uncertainties: Crowded credit with Tsujimoto, Korsmeyer, Cleary and Strasser.
Overlap with the earlier apoptosis prize may reduce the perceived novelty of recognition.
